entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Enentarzi was a chief-priest of Lagash for the god Ningirsu, serving as Ensi (governor) from approximately 2350 to 2300 BCE. He played a crucial role in the governance of Sumerian city-states and contributed significantly to the development of early urban societies.

Enentarzi's legacy can be seen in the continued worship of Ningirsu throughout ancient Mesopotamia, as well as the influence of his administrative reforms on subsequent city-state governments. His contributions to the cultural and political landscape of Sumer have had a lasting impact on the history of human civilization.

The extent of Enentarzi's personal life remains unknown, but his significance in the annals of ancient Mesopotamian history is undeniable.
